content:
Let the roots be \(x,y,z\in(0,1)\). Then
\[
x+y+z=1,\qquad a=xy+yz+zx,\qquad b=xyz.
\]
We maximize
\[
F=7(xy+yz+zx)-9xyz.
\]

At an interior critical point, Lagrange multipliers give
\[
7(y+z)-9yz=7(x+z)-9xz=7(x+y)-9xy.
\]
Subtracting pairs:
\[
(x-y)(7-9z)=0,\quad (y-z)(7-9x)=0,\quad (z-x)(7-9y)=0.
\]
Thus at least two variables are equal. Let \(y=z=t\), so \(x=1-2t\), with \(0<t<\frac12\). Then
\[
F(t)=7(2t-3t^2)-9(t^2-2t^3)=14t-30t^2+18t^3.
\]
\[
F'(t)=14-60t+54t^2=2(27t^2-30t+7).
\]
The critical points are
\[
t=\frac13,\quad t=\frac79.
\]
Only \(t=\frac13\) is in \((0,\frac12)\), giving \(x=y=z=\frac13\), and
\[
F=7\cdot \frac13-9\cdot \frac1{27}=2.
\]

On the boundary, the maximum is at most \(7/4\), so the interior value \(2\) is the global maximum.

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
